title: Hospital tote-induct or site-flow disruption with AGV state anomalies
user_facing_summary: Use this path when a hospital station cannot add or induct totes, a robot appears shut down, or the site cannot start or sustain sort. Confirm the observable impact, check for AGV location or tote-association anomalies, consider the source-supported service and lane recovery path, and validate tote flow and site operation.
playbook_goal: Restore safe hospital tote flow and broader site operation by distinguishing a localized hospital workflow problem from an AGV/tote-state or service-related disruption, applying only authorized high-level recovery actions, and validating stable operation.
observed_entry_symptoms: Hospital station cannot add or induct totes.
Totes can be removed but cannot be added at the hospital area.
A robot or AGV is reported in a shut down state.
The site cannot start sort or goes down during sort.
Hospital backlog or abnormal tote flow to the hospital area is reported.
negative_or_absent_signals: The source does not provide a confirmed root cause.
The source does not provide readable live service-status values or named service states.
The source does not establish that every reported AGV location anomaly caused the site-wide disruption.
Several screenshots have unreadable labels or ambiguous color meanings.

Possible AGV hospital-station server or OptiSweep service abnormality.
Possible downstream tote-flow disruption associated with tipper operation during recovery.
internal_pattern_notes: These are tentative patterns from chat, work-order notes, and recovery summaries. The source explicitly says the cause was not certain; none of these patterns should be treated as a confirmed diagnosis or required entry classification.
confidence_reason: The packet contains a clear symptom-to-diagnostic-to-recovery shape, including hospital induct failure, AGV/tote anomalies, service-reset context, API/Aveva-based recovery references, and validation reports. Confidence is limited by fragmented chronology, second-hand statements, unreadable screenshots, and uncertainty about the actual cause and exact service actions.

nodes.title: Check for AGV location, roster, and tote-association anomalies
nodes.intent: Determine whether the reported hospital-flow problem coincides with an AGV in an unexpected location, duplicate occupancy, disconnected tote, or residual tote association.
nodes.goal: Determine whether the reported hospital-flow problem coincides with an AGV in an unexpected location, duplicate occupancy, disconnected tote, or residual tote association.

nodes.needed_runbook_capability: Procedure needed to compare the affected AGV or robot location and rack occupancy with the expected fleet or station state using the source-referenced HMI/layout view, the source-supported operational view or fleet status view, and API/Aveva state view when available; the procedure should also identify residual or disconnected tote associations without prescribing data mutations.
nodes.expected_or_observed_result: Site operator or support user observes the physical or displayed AGV state using the available HMI/layout view, the source-supported operational view or fleet view when available, and the source-referenced API/Aveva state-management interface. Healthy signal: AGVs occupy expected locations and no disconnected or residual tote association is reported. Unhealthy signal: an AGV is reported in an unexpected location, multiple AGVs appear under one rack or in one location, an AGV is absent from an expected rack, or a disconnected/associated tote remains in the system. Inconclusive: identifiers, locations, or tote associations cannot be confirmed from the available view.
